messages:
Ajay: heads up — found a weird accounting gap with sidecar sampling + truncation. background embed requests sampled at 10% are showing small non-zero charges even when the client cancels before any token is emitted.
Maria: wait — sidecar background embeds charge before stream start? that sounds like the provisional vs confirmed debate we've had. :eyes:
Ajay: looks like we credit the ledger as soon as the routing sidecar hands the request off to the embed worker. if the client disconnects during handshake/truncation we still emit a provisional token record that never gets reconciled away.
Kei: can you paste the log lines?
Ajay: sure — snippet:
```
router(sidecar): dispatched sample req id=sr-9a3 route=bg-embed sample_rate=0.1
embed-worker: recv sr-9a3, estimated_tokens=8
router(sidecar): client closed stream before first token, marking truncated=true
ledger: write provisional {route:bg-embed, tokens:8, sample_rate:0.1, provisional:true}
```
Paul: aha — we multiply tokens by 1/sample_rate when showing charge (to estimate full batch) so that 8 * 10 = 80 visible tokens. when truncated we never confirm so provisional stays.
Maria: so customers see a tiny charge balloon because of scaling up the sample? yikes.
Ajay: yeah. costs are real in ledger (we double-count on recon) and console shows a spike.
billing-bot: automatic alert: provisional-write-rate for bg-embed route > baseline by 15%
Kei: two separate problems: 1) we stash provisional rows w/o a TTL/recon job, 2) the console shows sampled-estimates as actual charged tokens.
Paul: proposed short-term fix: don't scale-up sampled tokens until confirmation. store raw_sampled_tokens and display "sampled_estimate (not billed)" in console until ledger flips to confirmed.
Maria: UX ask: console needs an explicit column for sample_rate and truncation flag. customers and support should see raw vs scaled. right now the graph is misleading.
Ajay: agree. also we need a ledger cleanup job to sweep stale provisional rows after X minutes and apply zero-charge rollbacks if no confirm.
Kei: would that affect other provisional flows (stream retries, toolcalls)? we must be careful — some provisional writes are expected to be reconciled later.
Paul: yes, we need a reconciliation policy based on request_type. For background-sampled embeds we can safely treat provisional as tentative and auto-reverse after 5m. For toolcalls/interactive streams we keep current window.
Maria: long-term: add sample-aware attribution in aggregation pipeline. i.e. store both sampled_count and sample_rate; pipeline computes expected_token_exposure but UI shows both expected and actual billed.
Ajay: technical ask: minimal change to internal API — add headers: `X-Sample-Rate: 0.1` and `X-Truncated: true|false` and let ledger accept sampled_tokens/rate instead of already-scaling.
Kei: that breaks the current ledger schema which expects `tokens` int. schema change required.
Paul: alternative: keep tokens but add metadata JSON blob column `meta_sample_rate` (string) to ledger. cheaper migration.
Maria: will support need to update the console query layer too. current per-route query uses tokens sum directly. we'll need to surface both `tokens` and `meta_sample_rate` and compute display values in the frontend.
Ajay: another corner: routing retries. if router resends a sampled request after timeout we might write two provisional rows for same client request id. need dedupe key: sample_origin_id or session-hash.
Kei: suggestion: include `client_req_id || '-' || sample_nonce` as dedupe key; router generates sample_nonce per sample dispatch.
Paul: also add a quick gauge in observability: provisional_sample_rows_per_min and stale_provisional_seconds distribution.
Maria: can we gate immediate UI change behind a feature flag so SRE+support can opt-in while we test?
Ajay: yep — console flag `show_sample_metadata` and API/ledger flag `sample_metadata_enabled`.
billing-bot: FYI: finance asked for a one-off export of anomalous spikes for last 48h.
Kei: action items I can take: 1) draft minimal ledger migration (meta column) 2) add header parsing in router 3) dedupe key plan.
Paul: I'll update console queries and add new column in the route dashboard for `sample_rate` + `truncated`.
Maria: I'll file a runbook for support describing how to interpret sampled vs billed lines and how to run the export.
Ajay: I'll prototype the cleanup job and a reconciliation heuristic: if provisional and route==bg-embed and age>5m and no confirm -> write reversal entry.
Kei: ok — timeline?
Paul: console changes + feature flag: 3d. ledger migration + router header: 2d. cleanup job + reconciler: 2d. runbook: 1d. total staggered rollout in one week.
Maria: ping me when you have the UI PR so we can hide it behind flag. also add unit tests for sample-rate math (no accidental scaling).
Ajay: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: task created: FIN-EXPORT-827 for finance export
